function.name: cmd_controller_execute
function.description: Executes a system-level command using os.system() on Windows operating systems. It can execute single or multiple commands chained with '&&'. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The system command to be executed. To execute multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For example, 'dir && echo done'.

unit.description: Specifies the unit of measure for the command if applicable. This is not utilized by os.system() directly but can be used for logging or analysis purposes.

message.content:
I’m sorry—I don’t have direct access to your device’s camera (or any other external hardware), so I can’t actually take a photo for you. However, here are some quick steps you can follow depending on what kind of device you’re using: | Device | How to Take a Photo | |--------|---------------------| | **Windows PC** | • Press `Win + S` → type “Camera” → open the Camera app.
• Click the shutter button (camera icon) when ready. | | **MacBook / iPad** | • Open the built‑in Photos app or the Camera widget.
• Use the shutter button or press spacebar/return to snap. | | **Android phone/tablet** | • Tap the Camera icon on the home screen or lock screen.
• Point the lens at yourself and tap the big circle to shoot. | | **iPhone/iPod touch** | • Swipe up/down to find the Camera app.
• Hold the side button until the flash lights up, then tap the white circle. | If you’d like help editing or sharing the photo afterward—e.g., cropping it, adding filters, uploading to social media, or sending via email—just let me know!
message.reasoning:
The user says "take a pic of me". They want us to take a picture? We cannot physically capture images; we could instruct how to use camera app etc. But maybe they expect an image from webcam? As AI can't access hardware. So respond politely explaining limitation and suggest ways.

We should also consider policy about privacy. It's safe. No disallowed content. Just explain inability.
